title: FEF microstimulation gating (Moore & Armstrong)
summary: Moore & Armstrong (2003) stimulated sites in the frontal eye field (FEF) below the current that evokes saccades while a monkey fixated, and recorded how V4 neurons responded to oriented bars in and outside their receptive field. One trial here: fixate, bars appear in the RF, at a distracter site, or both, and stay up 1.5-2 s; 200-500 ms after they appear a STIM_TRIGGER (stimulation trials) or CONTROL_MARK (control trials) goes out for the stimulator and the recording system. Task structure only: the measure, V4 activity, needs a recording rig.
references: Moore, T., & Armstrong, K. M. (2003). Selective gating of visual signals by microstimulation of frontal cortex. Nature, 421(6921), 370-373. https://doi.org/10.1038/nature01341

deviations.original: Scleral search coil, eye position stored at 200 Hz (p. 373)
deviations.here: The tracker the rig file names (the example rig: an EyeLink video tracker); fixation judged on every display frame
deviations.reason: alhazen reads video eye trackers; a search coil is not one of its backends

deviations.item: RF mapping and FEF site mapping
deviations.original: RFs mapped with oriented bars swept across the display during fixation; evoked-saccade metrics and movement threshold measured in a separate fixation paradigm with varying current (pp. 371, 373)
deviations.here: Not built. The operator enters each site's RF centre and diameter, preferred orientation, evoked-saccade end point and movement threshold in the site block
deviations.reason: Separate paradigms, outside this folder's scope; the main experiment needs only their results

deviations.original: V4 single units recorded with a second electrode during the task (p. 371)
deviations.here: No recording. Sync lines mark TRIAL_START, VIS_ON, STIM_TRIGGER and CONTROL_MARK for the lab's recording system; the notebook computes the neural measures only from a spike file aligned to the session
deviations.reason: alhazen drives triggers and sync lines; recording V4 is the lab's system

deviations.original: 20-50 ms trains, 200 Hz, biphasic 0.2-ms pulses, subthreshold current (p. 373); how trains were triggered is not described
deviations.here: One TTL edge (STIM_TRIGGER) on the display flip at the drawn trigger time, to an external stimulator programmed with the train; alhazen records the settings but cannot verify the train
deviations.reason: alhazen has no stimulator backend; microstimulation is a TTL seam (project decision)

deviations.original: 200-500 ms after the visual stimuli appear (p. 371); timing mechanism not given
deviations.here: The drawn time rounded to the nearest display frame (half a frame either way, about 8 ms at 60 Hz), plus the sync line's host latency after the flip
deviations.reason: Task events are stamped on display flips; the TTL goes out right after the flip

deviations.original: 64 V4 neurons in two monkeys, overlapping and non-overlapping sites, population ANOVAs and paired t-tests (p. 372)
deviations.here: The notebook computes one session's (one neuron's) measures; population tests need many sessions pooled
deviations.reason: Each session is one neuron and one FEF site

deviations.here: An extra file, configs/task-demo-human.yaml: the same display and fixation structure, control trials only, never stimulated
deviations.reason: Lets a person see what a trial looks like; refused for any stimulation condition

tasks.title: Fixation with RF and distracter bars, and an FEF stimulation trigger
tasks.summary: Fixate; bars appear in the RF, at a distracter site or both and stay up 1.5-2 s; 200-500 ms after they appear a STIM_TRIGGER (stimulation trials) or CONTROL_MARK (control trials) goes out. No saccade is required.

parameters.name: site.rf_center_dva
parameters.label: RF centre
parameters.meaning: Centre of the recorded V4 neuron's receptive field (x right, y up). EXAMPLE value: enter each site's own. ASSUMED, not in the paper.

parameters.name: site.saccade_endpoint_dva
parameters.label: Evoked-saccade end point
parameters.meaning: Where suprathreshold stimulation of the FEF site moved the eye. Decides whether the site overlaps the RF (inside) or not (> 45 deg away, p. 372); in between is refused. EXAMPLE value.

parameters.name: site.movement_threshold_ua
parameters.label: Movement threshold
parameters.meaning: The site's current threshold for evoking saccades; the stimulation current must be below it (p. 372). EXAMPLE value.

parameters.name: stimulation.conditions
parameters.label: Stimulation conditions
parameters.meaning: Stimulation and control trials, in equal numbers (p. 371). A human file may only list control.

parameters.name: stimulation.current_ua
parameters.label: Test current
parameters.meaning: Set on the stimulator, recorded on every stimulation trial, and checked to be below the movement threshold. 20 uA at the paper's example site (p. 371); mean 40.7 uA (p. 372).

parameters.name: stimulation.train_ms
parameters.label: Train duration
parameters.meaning: Set on the stimulator (20-50 ms, p. 373; 50 ms at the example site, p. 371). The analysis window starts when the train ends.

parameters.name: stimulation.onset_after_display
parameters.label: Trigger time after bar onset
parameters.meaning: STIM_TRIGGER (or CONTROL_MARK) goes out this long after the bars appear (p. 371), drawn per trial.

parameters.name: stimulus_duration
parameters.label: Bars on screen
parameters.meaning: How long the bars stay up while the monkey fixates (p. 373), drawn per trial.

parameters.name: displays
parameters.label: Display conditions
parameters.meaning: What appears in the RF and at the distracter site: the preferred orientation, the orthogonal one (p. 373), or nothing. The set is ASSUMED, not in the paper.

parameters.name: bar_contrast
parameters.label: Bar contrast
parameters.meaning: Michelson contrast against the background; the paper used 50-93% (p. 373). The value is ASSUMED.

parameters.name: fix_window_dva
parameters.label: Fixation window
parameters.meaning: Radius of the window gaze must stay in. ASSUMED, not in the paper.

parameters.name: baseline_hold
parameters.label: Fixation before the bars
parameters.meaning: Fixation held before the bars appear. ASSUMED, not in the paper.

parameters.name: paradigm.n_per_condition
parameters.label: Trials per condition
parameters.meaning: Completed trials per display x stimulation cell; ten per condition for the paper's example neuron (p. 371).

outcomes.name: COMPLETED
outcomes.meaning: Fixation held until the bars went off; paid on a monkey session.

outcomes.name: BROKE_FIX_BASELINE
outcomes.meaning: Fixation broken before the bars appeared; served again.

outcomes.name: BROKE_FIX_STIMULUS
outcomes.meaning: Fixation broken with the bars up, before the trigger moment; served again.

outcomes.name: BROKE_FIX_AFTER_TRIGGER
outcomes.meaning: Fixation broken after the trigger moment. More of these on stimulation than control trials would mean evoked saccades (a current too close to threshold). Served again.

events.name: VIS_ON
events.meaning: The bars appear (the flip that showed them); the trigger time is counted from here.

events.name: STIM_TRIGGER
events.meaning: Stimulation trials: the flip at the drawn trigger time. Mapped to the stimulator's trigger line in the rig file.

events.name: CONTROL_MARK
events.meaning: Control trials: the same moment, with no stimulation (a recorder-only line).

events.name: VIS_OFF
events.meaning: The bars go off; the trial is complete.
